finding_dispositions.original_issue: P18 does not bind every build input. In scripts/check_accounting_proposal.py, the 'all candidate sources pinned' check inventories only .tex, .bib, .sty and .cls files beneath the manuscript directory. An included image, CSV table or TeX input outside that directory can be omitted from source_files. Changing that input then leaves the checker pins unchanged, so proposal_gate can continue reporting readiness for a stale candidate. Repair: capture and validate actual build dependencies, including figures, data and external project inputs; bind their hashes into acceptance. Explicitly identify environment-managed dependencies separately. Add a regression where an omitted included figure or external input changes and readiness closes.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: P1 — Preflight verification runs outside the preservation and attribution window. In Master.execute_phase, check_phase(phase, preflight) executes before creating the phase entry inventory and before any pre-edit preservation or capture_phase_changes call. A checker that accidentally overwrites or deletes an editable manuscript file can therefore alter the baseline subsequently preserved for a new phase. On resume, preflight changes likewise fall outside the recorded work window. check_protection protects frozen evidence, but does not restore or attribute ordinary editable files. Repair: preserve and persist the entry inventory before preflight; wrap preflight in its own preserved before-snapshot and finally-based contribution capture; enforce deletion obligations and pass its changes to subsequent planning and review. Alternatively, enforce and verify a strictly read-only preflight with prior-byte preservation. Add regression coverage for preflight overwrite, deletion and failure after a write.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: P2 — Partial-continuation freshness omits declared verification inputs. Master.save_continuation hashes contributed files, the test file and deliverables, but does not include checked['input_hashes']. In contrast, save_pending_review includes those inputs. phase_recovery then labels a continuation 'checked_snapshot_not_acceptance' solely from the incomplete evidence_hashes map. Changing a declared research or other checker input that is neither a contribution nor a deliverable leaves that label unchanged and supplies the next plan with stale checked-snapshot guidance. Repair: include declared check inputs in the continuation fingerprint and compare their current hashes with the values recorded by verification; record changed or missing inputs as requiring recheck. Bind the saved check record as well. Add a regression where only a declared checker input changes between partial work and recovery.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: Persisted process identity is not bound to a host boot. process_identity records only pid, state, pgid and start_ticks; Master.recover_process and _stop_recovered_group establish ownership using pid, pgid and start_ticks. Linux start_ticks measures time since boot, so after a reboot an unrelated process-group leader can match a stale saved tuple. Recovery would then obtain valid pidfds for that unrelated group and STOP/KILL it. Pidfds stabilize the selected process but do not establish that it belongs to the previous invocation. Repair: durably record the Linux boot ID with the worker identity and compare it before inspecting or signalling saved PIDs. A different boot proves the prior local processes cannot remain alive; archive that record without signalling current processes. Records lacking a boot identity must fail closed or follow an explicitly reviewed migration.
finding_dispositions.reason: Repaired and exercised by focused regressions; exact code mechanism and test disposition are recorded in the adjudication. data/accounting-master/proposal-first-repair-20261004/review-adjudication.md

finding_dispositions.original_issue: Unresolved prohibited deletions can escape the continuation veto through an early repair exit. In execute_phase, outstanding_deletions raises MasterError, which is caught and followed by approve_phase_plan. If that call returns None, execute_phase returns before reaching its final outstanding_deletions check. Master.run can then schedule an independent eligible phase while preserved project files remain deleted. The protection interface covers frozen evidence and controls, not every editable file tracked by outstanding_deletions. Repair: enforce the outstanding-deletion invariant whenever a phase yields back to the scheduler, including failed/blocked replanning and other early returns. Preserve the deletion obligations and stop further phase execution until restoration; allow the current bounded repair path to attempt restoration first.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: P2 — reload_state silently reuses cached state when a previously existing state.json disappears. __init__ can load accepted phases and run history, but reload_state only replaces self.state when the file exists. If the checkpoint is accidentally removed before reload, validation checks the old in-memory copy and succeeds; a subsequent refresh/save recreates that copy as canonical state. This conceals checkpoint loss and can resurrect outdated acceptance or discard newer history if the instance's snapshot is older. Repair: distinguish a genuinely new controller from one that has observed or committed persisted state. Under the writer lock, veto a missing checkpoint after persistence has been observed; require explicit evidence-preserving recovery instead of silently saving cached state. Preserve normal first-run initialization.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: High — The write-scope check has an inventory blind spot. Master.worker derives touched paths exclusively from changes_since(), whose editable_files() excludes .codex, .agents, other configuration directories, and all data/accounting-master subdirectories except deliverables. The explicit control snapshot covers only four files, while protected_hashes() does not inventory prior master run records. An implementation worker can therefore accidentally create or modify excluded project configuration, or overwrite an earlier response/check record, without appearing in touched or violating the supplied protected hashes. This contradicts the declared document-only write scope and preservation of prior evidence. Repair by separating the preservation inventory from the forbidden-write inventory: snapshot and verify excluded persistent configuration and prior evidence, permit only explicitly identified supervisor-generated changes, and reject newly created forbidden files. Do not rely on the workspace-write sandbox to enforce phase-specific paths. Add regression coverage for an out-of-scope configuration write and mutation of an earlier run record.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: High — Integrity-check failures can be downgraded into review unavailability. In Master.worker's finally block, only merge_hashes() errors are converted to ContinuationVeto. changes_since() calls editable_files(), which raises ValueError for a newly introduced symlink and can raise OSError for unreadable files. These exceptions bypass the integrity-failure record and reach phase_review(), which catches ValueError/OSError as review_unavailable, launches a retry, and eventually records ReviewPending. For example, replacing an ordinary editable document with a symlink during a review produces an integrity-verification exception instead of the required continuation veto. Repair by wrapping the entire post-worker integrity assessment, converting inventory/hash/scope-inspection failures into ContinuationVeto, and preserving the original worker exception plus verification error where recording remains possible. A verification failure must prohibit retry and further scheduling. Add regression coverage for a review that introduces a symlink and for an inventory read failure.
finding_dispositions.reason: Repaired and exercised by focused regressions; exact code mechanism and test disposition are recorded in the adjudication. data/accounting-master/proposal-first-repair-20261004/review-adjudication.md

finding_dispositions.original_issue: P18 does not establish that its PDF was built from the pinned source bytes. In scripts/check_accounting_proposal.py, anchor() verifies current hashes, while the recorder check verifies only dependency paths. build.exit_code, the build log and rendered_pdf_sha256 do not bind the PDF to source hashes observed during that build. An ordinary stale-build case therefore passes the structural checks: retain an earlier PDF, recorder and rendered pages; edit main.tex or an included figure; update its source_files hash; and submit the new manuscript manifest. All current checks can succeed although the rendered review concerns an earlier source version. Repair by preserving a build-time record containing the actual input hashes and resulting PDF hash, and require those hashes to match the current candidate. Capture inputs around the successful build and reject changed inputs; bind rendering to that recorded PDF. Add a regression that edits and re-pins a source or figure without rebuilding and requires P18 to fail. The supplied interfaces do not identify another component that already enforces this build-time binding.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: P1 — Verification input hashes can be replaced by current hashes without detecting stale verification. In scripts/run_accounting_master.py, check_phase validates the raw checker capture but never verifies result['input_hashes']. save_pending_review uses only their names and calls evidence_hashes to snapshot current bytes; final acceptance does the same. Consequently, if a checker reports hashes for inputs it checked and those inputs subsequently change during verification, the checkpoint binds the changed bytes while retaining the earlier passing result. Later checkpoint verification passes because it compares against that new snapshot. save_continuation explicitly detects this mismatch, but the acceptance path does not. Repair: compare every declared input hash with the current file before pending-review creation and acceptance, and reject/recheck mismatches without rebasing them. Preserve the checker’s original hash mapping as the verification binding. Add a regression where a passing checker reports an old input digest after that input changes; neither acceptance nor resumable accepted-check status should result.
finding_dispositions.reason: Repaired and exercised by focused regressions; exact code mechanism and test disposition are recorded in the adjudication. data/accounting-master/proposal-first-repair-20261004/review-adjudication.md

finding_dispositions.original_issue: P2 — Recovery omits the latest failed replan review. execute_phase writes repair plans and their reviews beneath replan-N directories, but phase_recovery in scripts/accounting_master_support.py searches plan_review only at the attempt root and its direct review_plan-retry directories. If an initial plan passes, implementation fails, and a subsequent replan receives REVISE or BLOCKED, recovery can present the original AGREE as the recent plan review. The root approved-plan.json also remains the previous approved plan when replanning fails. This gives the next planning pass stale structured navigation precisely when it needs the latest repair findings. Repair: discover replan-N plan responses and reviews, including their retries, and distinguish the latest proposed/rejected plan from the latest approved plan. Preserve their ordering explicitly or select consistently across those directories. Add a regression covering failed replanning followed by recovery in a new invocation.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: In bounded_process, the waitid condition observes exit before checking the deadline. If the child remains active past seconds but exits before the next polling iteration, the loop ends with reason=None. The same bypass occurs if on_spawn consumes the remaining budget and the child exits before polling starts. An exit code of zero can therefore make an over-budget attempt indistinguishable from an ordinary successful attempt, undermining the stated rule that timed-out outputs cannot become implementation responses. Repair: observe exit and elapsed time together, conservatively classify an exit first observed at or after the deadline as timeout, and retain that classification through cleanup. Check elapsed time after registration as well. Add focused coverage for exit between the last pre-deadline poll and the next observation, and for registration consuming the deadline; verify both preserve outputs without treating the attempt as successful.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: Blocked responses lose their actionable findings. In execute_phase, both the work['verdict'] == 'BLOCKED' branch and the ordinary response['verdict'] == 'BLOCKED' branch update status, issues and residuals but omit next_actions. The partial-review BLOCKED branch correctly saves next_actions. Consequently an external block can leave the phase's previous next_actions intact, or retain none, while subsequent refreshes construct the next plan from that record. Repair both branches to persist the current response's next_actions, replacing stale values even when the new list is empty. Verify that the refreshed plan and a resumed invocation expose the actual unblock instructions.

finding_dispositions.original_issue: Run finalization is not protected against an ordinary handled interruption. Master.run catches KeyboardInterrupt in its main try, but its finally block performs refresh/save, plan publication, manifest publication and event writing outside that handler. The nested finalization handler catches only ContinuationVeto, ValueError and OSError. A SIGTERM translated to KeyboardInterrupt during final refresh or terminal publication therefore escapes to the module entrypoint, potentially leaving the manifest without finished_at/outcome and leaving the previous executable next plan published. A second interruption while finalizing an already interrupted run has the same problem. Repair this with a bounded, signal-deferred finalization section that durably records interruption and either publishes a verified current plan or a non-executable recovery record before restoring signal handling. Preserve the existing worker-cleanup guarantees. Verify interruption during final refresh and terminal publication, including interruption after a prior stop.
finding_dispositions.reason: Repaired and exercised by focused regressions; exact code mechanism and test disposition are recorded in the adjudication. data/accounting-master/proposal-first-repair-20261004/review-adjudication.md

finding_dispositions.original_issue: REVISE: Persisted state does not bind the complete phase catalog. Master.__init__ stores only workflow_sha256, and verify_workflow() compares only catalog['workflow']. A change to a pending phase's deps, criteria, deliverables, checker, retry_inputs, or other phase contract can therefore pass validate_state(), pass verify_workflow(), and be scheduled by refresh() under a newly reviewed-looking contract. The accepted-phase path partially detects contract changes via accepted_phase_hash, but pending and non-accepted phases have no equivalent protection. This violates stale-state handling and can execute a phase from a catalog different from the one that produced the checkpoint. Repair by persisting a canonical full-catalog hash (or per-phase contract hashes) in state at creation and checking it before refresh/eligibility; reject with an explicit migration ContinuationVeto on mismatch. If intentional migrations are needed, require a reviewed migration record that preserves prior evidence and rebinds every affected phase. Add a regression covering a persisted pending phase whose criteria/dependencies/checker changes and asserting scheduling is vetoed until migration.
finding_dispositions.reason: Catalog already invalidates current controller review, pending-check and accepted-phase identities; dedicated regression verifies this. data/accounting-master/proposal-first-repair-20261004/review-adjudication.md

finding_dispositions.original_issue: scripts/run_accounting_master.py — validate_response performs set membership on value['verdict'] before checking its type. A response containing all required fields but a list or object verdict raises TypeError ('unhashable type'), rather than MasterError. _worker_result has the same problem earlier in response.get('verdict') in {'REVISE', 'BLOCKED'}. phase_review catches MasterError, ValueError and OSError, so this malformed response bypasses the promised bounded retry and ReviewPending recovery. Repair both sites by checking that the verdict is a string before set membership, and classify invalid verdict types as MasterError. Add focused coverage for list/object verdicts demonstrating preservation of the rejected response, a fresh read-only retry, and ReviewPending after two invalid responses.
